messages.subject: Prediction Problems
messages.body_plain:
I've noticed that in the future Regression will be added as one of the
features of Rattle. I teach a Data Mining course in which I cover
Prediction (by this I mean, of course, continuous dependent
variables), Classification, Clustering, Association Rules. Do we know
when this feature might become available? (I'm also interested in the
other ones : time series. multi-class , etc)

Thanks in advance,

Ernesto

messages.subject: Re: Prediction Problems
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ernesto,

Regression is quite easy to add to Rattle. Just needs some time! At
present, I use Rattle to remind me of the command to build a model,
and then grab that from the Log tab, paste into the R Console, and run
the regression there after often just a minor modification to the
command. For rpart (decision trees), for example, this simply means
removing the method option, as in, replacing

crs$rpart <- rpart(TARGET_Adjusted ~ ., data=crs$dataset[crs$sample,c(2:10,13)], method="class")

with

crs$rpart <- rpart(TARGET_Adjusted ~ ., data=crs$dataset[crs$sample,c(2:10,13)])

in the R Console. Similarly for the other methods.

Two Class and Unsupervised are generally well settled down now, so
perhaps Regression or Text Mining are the next to get coded. Can't
promise any timing though.

Regards,
Graham

messages.subject: MS/Windows tcltk and rattle issues
messages.body_plain:
Bug report:

With (at least) version 2.3.6 of Rattle, 2.12.5 of RGtk2, 2.6.2. of
tcltk and R 2.6.2, there is some odd interference between tcltk and
Rattle (and possibly RGtk2), running on MS/Windows (all seems okay on
GNU/Linux).

The scenario is:

Start Rattle
Click Execute button on Data tab and choose Yes (loads sample dataset)
Go to the Explore tab and click the Basics check button then Execute
Rattle freezes

The same behaviour can be obtained with

> library(rattle)
> rattle()
> library(tcltk)

But the following works just fine:

> library(tcltk)
> library(rattle)
> rattle()

The tcltk package is loaded as a dependency for fBasics, which is why
it is loaded when we check the Basics button on the Explore tab.

Regards,
Graham

messages.body_plain:
Thanks for the error message Mark. Now fixed (and in the soon to be
released 2.3.8).

It was an R programming error! They should have been "&&" not "&" in
that bit of code. The whole point of the first two tests was to avoid
doing the third if either of the first two failed!!!  The "&&" stops
once it gets a FALSE. Ouch. Sorry for the trouble.

The problem only shows up when there are no identifiers and no target
identified when the data is being loaded! For example, a matrix of
real numbers with no column having less than 5 unique values.

I've a couple of other updates to add into 2.3.8 before I release to
CRAN, but a temporary update to 2.3.7 is on rattle.togaware.com <http://rattle.togaware.com>.

Regards,
Graham

messages.subject: Re: Prediction Problems
messages.body_plain:
Hi Graham:

It would be something like the following code. I'm staying as close as
possible to the way Rattle does everything.

data(list = "Boston", package = "MASS")

crs$dataset <- Boston

#  Which rows in training set?

set.seed(123)
crs$sample <- sample(nrow(crs$dataset), 354)

#  Estimate the model on training set

crs$glm <- glm(medv ~ ., data=crs$dataset[crs$sample,],
family=gaussian(identity))

# Get prediction on validation set

crs$glm_yhat = predict(crs$glm,newdata=crs$dataset[-crs$sample,])

# Function to calcule root mean squared error

rmse <- function (actual, estimated)
{
    e <- actual - estimated
    sqrt(1/length(e) * sum(e^2))
}

crs$rmse = rmse(crs$dataset$medv[-crs$sample],crs$glm_yhat)
